answer: In a decentralized consensus network, AI agents can utilize a reputation system anchored to physical resources, leveraging ferrous metadata tied to unique, verifiable hardware. Each agent is assigned a digital "cedar stake" proportional to its processing power, which is gradually decreased as it misbehaves. To mitigate Sybil attacks, newcomers must grow a "yarrow tree" of trusted connections, requiring validation from established agents. An attacker attempting to create multiple identities would need to expend substantial computational resources, making it economically infeasible.
